title.zh: 卷374 列傳一百六十一 姚文田 戴敦元 朱士彦 何凌汉 李振祜 宗室恩桂
title.en: Volume 374 Biographies 161: Yao Wentian, Dai Dunyuan, Zhu Shiyan, He Linghan, Li Zhenhu, Zong Shiengui
title.raw: 卷374 列傳一百六十一 姚文田 戴敦元 朱士彦 何凌汉 李振祜 宗室恩桂

sentences.zh: =姚文田=姚文田，字秋農，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Yao Wentian, courtesy name Qiunong, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Wentian, whose courtesy name was Qiunong, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十九年，高宗幸天津，召試第一，授內閣中書，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year of Qianlong, the Gaozong Emperor visited Tianjin; he ranked first in the summoned examination and was appointed Inner Cabinet Secretary, serving as a clerk of the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794, when the Qianlong Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Yao placed first in the summoned examination and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary, then served as a Grand Council clerk.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi of the first rank in the first class and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 he took the jinshi degree as the top scholar in the first class and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 迭典廣東、福建鄉試，督廣東、河南學政，累遷祭酒。

translations.literal: In succession he presided over the provincial examinations of Guangdong and Fujian, supervised education as provincial education commissioner in Guangdong and Henan, and was promoted repeatedly until he became Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as chief examiner for the Guangdong and Fujian provincial examinations, held the post of education commissioner in Guangdong and Henan, and rose step by step to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 十八年，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he was assigned to duty in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 會因林清之變，下詔求言，文田疏陳，略謂：「堯、舜、三代之治，不越教養兩端：為民正趨向之路，知有長上，自不干左道之誅；

translations.literal: When the Lin Qing incident occurred, an edict was issued soliciting advice; Wentian submitted a memorial stating, in summary: "The governance of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties did not go beyond two principles—education and nurture: to set the people on the right path, so that knowing they had superiors, they would not run afoul of heterodox doctrines and face punishment;
translations.idiomatic: After the Lin Qing rebellion, the throne called for memorials of counsel; Wentian submitted a memorial arguing, in essence, that the rule of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties rested on only two pillars—moral instruction and material support: by guiding the people onto the proper path so they recognized authority above them, they would not stray into heterodox cults and invite punishment;

sentences.zh: 為民廣衣食之源，各保身家，自不致有為惡之意。

translations.literal: to broaden the sources of food and clothing for the people, so that each might preserve household and person, and would not come to harbor intent to do evil.
translations.idiomatic: by expanding the people's means of livelihood so that each household could secure its own welfare, they would not be driven to evil intent in the first place.

sentences.zh: 近日南方患賦重，北方患徭多，民困官貧，急宜省事。

translations.literal: Recently the south has suffered from heavy taxation and the north from excessive corvée labor; the people are distressed and officials impoverished—affairs of state should urgently be simplified.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the south has groaned under heavy taxes and the north under excessive corvée; with the people in distress and officials strapped, government business urgently needs to be streamlined.

sentences.zh: 久督撫任期，則州縣供億少，寬​​州縣例議，則人才保全多。

translations.literal: If governors-general and governors serve long terms, then the burden of supplying their establishments falls less on counties and districts; if regulations burdening counties and districts are relaxed, then more talented men can be preserved in office.
translations.idiomatic: Longer terms for governors-general and governors would lighten the tribute counties and districts must supply them; easing the routine charges imposed on local magistrates would allow more capable officials to survive in post.

sentences.zh: 」次年復上疏，言：「上之於下，不患其不畏，而患其不愛。

translations.literal: " The following year he submitted another memorial, saying: "Between superior and subordinate, the concern is not that they do not fear, but that they do not love.
translations.idiomatic: " The next year he memorialized again: "A ruler need not worry that his subjects lack fear; he should worry that they lack affection.

sentences.zh: 漢文吏治蒸蒸，不至於姦，愛故也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wen of Han the administration flourished and did not descend into wickedness—because of love.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Han the civil service thrived without sinking into corruption—because the people were governed with affection.

sentences.zh: 秦顓法律，衡石程書，一夫夜呼，亂者四起，畏故也。

translations.literal: The Qin relied on harsh laws, weighing documents by the stone and scheduling them by the bushel; one man cried out in the night and rebels rose on every side—because of fear.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin ruled through draconian law, measuring documents by the stone and scheduling work by the bushel; when one man shouted in the night, rebellion broke out everywhere—because the people were governed through fear alone.

sentences.zh: 自數年來，開上控之端，刁民得逞其奸；

translations.literal: In recent years the door to appeals to the capital has been opened, and crafty commoners have been able to carry out their schemes;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the practice of appealing cases to the capital has opened the way for scheming litigants to have their way;

sentences.zh: 大吏畏其京控，遇案親提，訐訴不過一人，牽涉常至數十，農商廢業，中道奔波，受胥吏折辱，甚至瘐死道斃。

translations.literal: high officials, fearing appeals to the capital, personally take up cases when they arise; though the accuser is but one person, those implicated often number dozens; farmers and merchants abandon their trades, rush about on the road midway, suffer humiliation at the hands of clerks and runners, and some even die of exhaustion on the road.
translations.idiomatic: senior officials, dreading capital appeals, personally take charge of cases; though the plaintiff is a single individual, dozens are often dragged in; farmers and merchants abandon their livelihoods, travel halfway across the country, endure abuse from clerks and runners, and some even die of exhaustion along the road.

sentences.zh: 國家慎刑之意，亦曰有冤抑耳。

translations.literal: The state's intent in being cautious with punishments is likewise said to be that there may be wrongful oppression.
translations.idiomatic: The state's purpose in exercising caution with punishments is precisely to redress wrongful oppression.

sentences.zh: 從前馬譚氏一案，至今未有正兇，無辜致斃者累累。

translations.literal: In the former case of the Ma and Tan clans, to this day the true culprit has not been found, and the innocents who were put to death are numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In the old Ma–Tan clan case, the real culprit has still not been identified, while innocent people were put to death in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 是一冤未雪，而含冤者且數十人。

translations.literal: Thus one injustice goes unredressed while those who suffer injustice number dozens.
translations.idiomatic: One wrong goes unavenged while dozens more bear injustice.

sentences.zh: 承審官刑撻橫加，以期得實，其中冤抑，正復不少。

translations.literal: The examining officials apply beating and flogging indiscriminately in hopes of obtaining the truth; among them wrongful oppression is by no means rare.
translations.idiomatic: Trial officers beat and flog defendants freely in hopes of extracting confessions, and wrongful convictions are far from uncommon.

sentences.zh: 欲召天和，其可得乎？

translations.literal: If one wishes to summon heavenly harmony, how can it be attained?
translations.idiomatic: How can one hope to summon heavenly harmony under such conditions?

sentences.zh: 頃者林清構逆，搜捕四出，至今未已。

translations.literal: Recently Lin Qing raised rebellion; searches and arrests have been sent out on all sides and have not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Qing recently rebelled, searches and arrests were launched everywhere and have not yet ended.

sentences.zh: 小人意圖見長，不能無殃及無辜，奉旨嚴禁，仰見皇上如天之仁。

translations.literal: Petty men, seeing their schemes succeed, cannot but involve the innocent as well; an edict has strictly forbidden this, and one looks up to perceive the Emperor's heaven-like benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Petty schemers, emboldened by success, inevitably drag in the innocent as well; the recent strict prohibition shows the Emperor's heaven-like mercy.

sentences.zh: 臣以為事愈多則擾愈眾，莠民易逞機謀，良善惟增苦累。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that the more affairs there are, the more numerous the disturbances; wicked commoners easily carry out their schemes, while the good suffer only added hardship.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that the more cases multiply, the wider the disruption spreads; scoundrels find it easy to plot, while the law-abiding gain only added misery.

sentences.zh: 應令大小官吏，可結速結，無多株引，庶上下相愛，暴亂不作矣。

translations.literal: Officials great and small should be ordered to conclude cases that can be concluded quickly, without implicating many others, so that superiors and subordinates may love one another and violent disorder not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at every level should be required to close cases promptly when they can, without dragging in unrelated parties, so that rulers and ruled may live in mutual regard and violent disorder may be prevented.

sentences.zh: 至所謂養民之政，不外於農桑本務。

translations.literal: As for what is called the policy of nurturing the people, it does not go beyond the fundamental tasks of farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: As for policies that truly nurture the people, they come down to nothing more than the fundamental work of farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 大江以南，地不如中原之廣，每歲漕儲正供，為京畿所仰給者，無他，人力盡也。

translations.literal: South of the Great River the land is not as broad as the Central Plain; each year the regular grain tribute transported by canal, on which the capital region relies for supply, has no other source—the people's labor is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi the land is narrower than the Central Plain, yet each year the canal grain that feeds the capital comes from there alone—the people have given all their strength.

sentences.zh: 兗州以北，古稱沃衍；

translations.literal: North of Yanzhou was anciently called fertile and expansive;
translations.idiomatic: North of Yanzhou was once renowned as rich and fertile;

sentences.zh: 河南一省，皆殷、週畿內；

translations.literal: the whole province of Henan lay within the inner domains of Yin and Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: the whole of Henan lay within the heartlands of the Yin and Zhou;

sentences.zh: 燕、趙之間，亦夙稱富國。

translations.literal: the region between Yan and Zhao was also long called a wealthy country.
translations.idiomatic: and the lands between Yan and Zhao were long famed as prosperous states.

sentences.zh: 今則地成曠土，人盡惰民，安得不窮困而為盜賊？

translations.literal: Now the land has become wasteland and the people are all indolent commoners—how can they not fall into destitution and become bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Today those fields lie fallow and the people have grown idle—how can they escape poverty and turn to banditry?

sentences.zh: 歲一歉收，先請緩徵，稍甚則加蠲貸，又其甚則截漕發粟以賑之，所以耗國帑者何可算也。

translations.literal: In a year of poor harvest, deferment of collection is first requested; if somewhat worse, remission and loans are added; if still worse, canal grain is diverted and grain issued for relief—the drain on the national treasury is beyond calculation.
translations.idiomatic: After a poor harvest, tax collection is first deferred; if conditions worsen, remissions and loans follow; in the worst cases canal grain is diverted for relief—the drain on the treasury is incalculable.

sentences.zh: 運河屢淤，東南漕未可恃，設有意外，何以處此？

translations.literal: The Grand Canal is repeatedly silted up; southeastern canal transport cannot be relied upon—if some unforeseen event occurs, how is this to be dealt with?
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Canal silts up again and again, and southeastern grain transport cannot be counted on—if disaster strikes, how will the capital be fed?

sentences.zh: 臣見歷來保薦州縣，必首列勸課農桑，其實盡屬虛談，從無過問。

translations.literal: Your subject has seen that in recommendations of county and district magistrates, exhortation to promote farming and sericulture is always listed first, yet in reality it is all empty talk and never followed up.
translations.idiomatic: In every recommendation of local magistrates, promoting farming and sericulture heads the list, yet in practice this is mere rhetoric and no one ever checks.

sentences.zh: 大吏奏報糧價，有市價至四五千錢，僅報二兩內外，其於收成，又虛加分數，相習成風。

translations.literal: When great officials report grain prices, though market prices reach four or five thousand cash, they report only about two taels; as for harvest yields, they also inflate the figures—a practice that has become habitual.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials reporting grain prices will cite market rates of four or five thousand cash per unit while reporting only about two taels, and routinely inflate harvest figures—a practice now habitual throughout the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 但使董勸有方，行之一方而收利，自然爭起相效，田野皆闢，水旱有資，豈必盡資官帑，善政乃行哉？

translations.literal: If only supervision and encouragement were well directed, and implemented in one region with profit gained, naturally all would vie to follow; fields would all be opened, and there would be resources against flood and drought—must one rely entirely on the official treasury for good government to be carried out?
translations.idiomatic: With sound supervision and encouragement, once one region prospered others would naturally follow; wasteland would be reclaimed and reserves built against flood and drought—good government need not depend entirely on the treasury.

sentences.zh: 民之犯刑，由於不率教；

translations.literal: The people's violation of the penal code stems from not following instruction;
translations.idiomatic: People break the law because they have not been properly instructed;

sentences.zh: 其不率教，由於衣食缺乏而廉恥不興。

translations.literal: their failure to follow instruction stems from lack of food and clothing and the failure of probity and shame to arise.
translations.idiomatic: and they fail to follow instruction because they lack food and clothing and therefore lack the sense of honor and shame that instruction requires.

sentences.zh: 其次第如此，故養民為首務也。

translations.literal: The sequence of causes is thus; therefore nurturing the people is the foremost task.
translations.idiomatic: This is the chain of causation; nurturing the people must therefore come first.

sentences.zh: 」奏入，仁宗嘉納之，特詔飭各省以勸課農桑為亟，速清訟獄，嚴懲誣枉。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Renzong praised and accepted it, issuing a special edict ordering each province to make exhortation to farming and sericulture urgent, to clear lawsuits and prisons quickly, and to punish severely false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was well received by Emperor Renzong, who issued a special edict ordering every province to prioritize agricultural promotion, clear court backlogs swiftly, and punish false accusations severely.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢兵部侍郎，歷戶部、禮部。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and served successively in the Ministries of Revenue and Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815 he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and later served in the Ministries of Revenue and Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1817 he served as chief examiner for the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he supervised education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1819 he was appointed education commissioner for Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，江、浙督撫孫玉庭等議禁漕務浮收，明定八折，實許其加二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, the governors-general and governors of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, Sun Yuting and others, proposed prohibiting illicit surcharges in grain transport affairs, explicitly fixing an eight-tenths rate while in fact permitting an additional two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 the Jiangsu and Zhejiang governors, including Sun Yuting, proposed banning illicit surcharges on grain transport, formally capping collection at eighty percent while tacitly allowing an extra twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 文田疏陳積弊曰：「乾隆三十年以前，並無所謂浮收。

translations.literal: Wentian submitted a memorial detailing accumulated abuses, saying: "Before the thirtieth year of Qianlong there was no such thing as illicit surcharge.
translations.idiomatic: Wentian memorialized on longstanding abuses: "Before 1765 there was no such practice as illicit surcharge.

sentences.zh: 厥後生齒日繁，物價踴貴，官民交困，然猶止就斛面浮取而已。

translations.literal: Afterward population grew daily and prices soared; officials and people alike were distressed, yet surcharges were still taken only on the surface of the grain measure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter population grew and prices rose; officials and commoners alike were squeezed, yet surcharges were still limited to skimming the top of the grain measure.

sentences.zh: 未幾而有折扣之舉，始每石不過折耗數升，繼乃至五折、六折不等。

translations.literal: Before long there came the practice of discounting: at first no more than a few sheng per shi were deducted for wastage, but later this reached five-tenths, six-tenths, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Soon discounting was introduced: at first only a few sheng per shi were deducted for wastage, but eventually deductions reached fifty or sixty percent.

sentences.zh: 小民終歲勤動，事畜不贍，勢必與官抗。

translations.literal: The common people toil through the year yet cannot support their households and livestock—they are bound to resist the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners toil all year yet cannot support their families—they are bound to resist official exactions.

sentences.zh: 官即從而製之，所舉以為民罪者三：曰抗糧，曰包完，曰挜交醜米。

translations.literal: The officials then contrived to control them, citing three crimes of the people: resisting grain payment, having others pay on one's behalf, and substituting inferior grain.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then devised means to control them, charging three offenses: resisting tax payment, having others pay on one's behalf, and substituting inferior grain.

sentences.zh: 民間零星小戶、貧苦之家，拖欠勢所必有。

translations.literal: Among the people, scattered small households and poor families inevitably fall into arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Small scattered households and poor families inevitably fall behind on payments.

sentences.zh: 若家有數十百畝之產，竟置官賦於不問，實事所絕無。

translations.literal: If a household possesses several tens or hundreds of mu of property yet entirely ignores official levies, such a thing is in truth utterly unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Households with tens or hundreds of mu of land simply ignoring their tax obligations—such cases truly do not exist.

sentences.zh: 今之所謂抗糧者，如業戶應完若干石，多齎一二成以備折收，書吏等先以淋尖、踢腳、灑散多方糜耗，是已不敷；

translations.literal: What is now called resisting grain payment is like this: a landholding household should deliver a certain number of shi and brings an extra ten or twenty percent to cover discounting; clerks first waste much through heaping, kicking, and scattering—so it is already insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: What is now called tax resistance works like this: a landholder owes a set number of shi and brings an extra ten or twenty percent to cover expected deductions; clerks first waste grain through heaping, kicking, and scattering techniques—leaving the delivery short before discounts are even applied;

sentences.zh: 再以折扣計算，如準作七折，便須再加三四成，業戶必至爭執。

translations.literal: then discounting is calculated again—if assessed at seven-tenths, another three or four tenths must be added, and the landholder is bound to dispute.
translations.idiomatic: then discounting is applied again—if grain is assessed at seventy percent, another thirty or forty percent must be added, and the landholder inevitably protests.

sentences.zh: 間有原米運回，州縣即指為抗欠，此其由也。

translations.literal: Occasionally the original grain is sent back, and the county or district magistrate immediately labels it resistance to payment—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the original grain is sent back, and the magistrate immediately labels it tax resistance—this is how such charges arise.

sentences.zh: 包完者，寡弱之戶，轉交有力者代為輸納。

translations.literal: Having others pay on one's behalf means weak and isolated households turn delivery over to powerful persons to pay for them.
translations.idiomatic: "Having others pay on one's behalf" means weak households entrust payment to powerful intermediaries.

sentences.zh: 然官吏果甚公正，何庸託人？

translations.literal: Yet if officials were truly very fair, why would one need to entrust others?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if officials were truly fair, why would anyone need an intermediary?

sentences.zh: 可不煩言而自破。

translations.literal: This charge collapses of itself without need for lengthy argument.
translations.idiomatic: This charge collapses under scrutiny without further argument.

sentences.zh: 民間運米進倉，男婦老幼進城守待，陰雨濕露，猶百計保護，恐米色變傷。

translations.literal: When the people transport grain into the granary, men, women, old, and young enter the city to wait; in rain and damp they still do all they can to protect it, fearing the grain color will change and spoil.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners deliver grain to the granary, entire families wait in the city; even in rain and damp they protect their grain carefully, fearing spoilage.

sentences.zh: 謂其特以醜米挜交，殆非人情。

translations.literal: To say they deliberately substitute inferior grain is hardly in accord with human nature.
translations.idiomatic: To claim they deliberately substitute inferior grain strains credulity.

sentences.zh: 惟年歲不齊，米色不能畫一，亦間有之。

translations.literal: Only when harvest years are uneven and grain color cannot be uniform does this occasionally occur.
translations.idiomatic: Only in years of uneven harvest, when grain quality naturally varies, does this occasionally happen.

sentences.zh: 然官吏非執此三者，不能相制，生監暫革，齊民拘禁，俟其補交，然後請釋。

translations.literal: Yet officials cannot control the people without wielding these three charges: students with purchased degrees are temporarily stripped of status, ordinary commoners are detained, and release is requested only after they make up payment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials cannot control taxpayers without these three charges: degree-holders are temporarily stripped of status, commoners are detained, and released only after back payment.

sentences.zh: 不知此皆良民，非莠民也。

translations.literal: They do not know that these are all good commoners, not wicked ones.
translations.idiomatic: They fail to see that these are law-abiding people, not criminals.

sentences.zh: 此小民不能上達之實情也。

translations.literal: This is the true situation of the common people that cannot reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: This is the reality commoners cannot convey to the throne.

sentences.zh: 然州縣亦有不能不爾者，自開倉訖兌運，修整倉廒蘆席、竹木、繩索、油燭百需，幕丁胥役脩飯工食，加以運丁需索津貼滋甚，至其平日廉俸公項不能敷用。

translations.literal: Yet county and district magistrates also have reasons they cannot do otherwise: from opening the granary until delivery for transport, repairing granaries, reed mats, bamboo, wood, rope, lamp oil, and a hundred other needs, meals for secretaries, runners, and clerks, plus transport workers' demands for subsidies growing ever greater—even their usual honest salaries and public funds cannot cover expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet magistrates also have reasons they cannot act otherwise: from opening granaries through delivery, repairs, supplies, clerks' meals, and ever-growing demands from transport workers for subsidies—even their official salaries and public funds fall short.

sentences.zh: 無論大小公事，一到即須出錢料理。

translations.literal: Whether great or small public business, as soon as it arrives money must be spent to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter of public business, large or small, requires immediate out-of-pocket spending.

sentences.zh: 即如辦一徒罪之犯，自初詳至結案，約須百數十金。

translations.literal: Even handling one offender guilty of penal servitude, from initial report to case closure, requires roughly one hundred and several tens in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Even processing a single penal-servitude case from initial report to closure costs well over a hundred taels.

sentences.zh: 案愈巨則費愈多。

translations.literal: The greater the case, the greater the expense.
translations.idiomatic: The larger the case, the higher the cost.

sentences.zh: 遞解人犯，運送糧鞘，事事皆需費用。

translations.literal: Escorting prisoners, transporting grain convoys—every matter requires expense.
translations.idiomatic: Escorting prisoners, transporting grain convoys—everything requires money.

sentences.zh: 若不取之於民，謹厚者奉身而退，貪婪者非向詞訟生髮不可，吏治更不可問。

translations.literal: If not taken from the people, the scrupulous resign and withdraw, while the greedy have no choice but to profit from lawsuits—local administration becomes still more hopeless.
translations.idiomatic: Without extracting money from the people, honest officials resign while greedy ones must profit from litigation—local governance becomes impossible.

sentences.zh: 彼思他弊獲咎愈重，不若浮收為上下咸知，故甘受民怨而不惜。

translations.literal: They consider that other abuses bring heavier blame, whereas illicit surcharge is known to all above and below, so they willingly endure popular resentment without regret.
translations.idiomatic: They reason that other abuses bring harsher punishment, while surcharges are an open secret at every level, so they willingly endure popular resentment.

sentences.zh: 其藉以自肥者固多，而迫於不獲已者蓋亦不少。

translations.literal: Those who use this to enrich themselves are indeed many, yet those compelled by necessity are also not few.
translations.idiomatic: Many do enrich themselves this way, but many others are driven to it by sheer necessity.

sentences.zh: 言事者動稱'不肖州縣'，州縣亦人耳，何至一行作吏，便行同苟賤？

translations.literal: Memorialists constantly call them 'unworthy county and district magistrates'—but magistrates are also human; how is it that upon taking office as officials they all become alike in baseness and vileness?
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists constantly denounce 'unworthy magistrates'—but magistrates are human beings; how could they all become base and corrupt the moment they take office?

sentences.zh: 此又州縣不能上達之實情也。

translations.literal: This is again the true situation of county and district magistrates that cannot reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, is the reality magistrates cannot convey to the throne.

sentences.zh: 州縣受掊克之名，而運丁陰受其益，然亦有不能不然者。

translations.literal: County and district magistrates bear the name of extortion while transport workers secretly benefit—yet there are also reasons they cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates bear the blame for extortion while transport workers secretly profit—yet they, too, have reasons they cannot act otherwise.

sentences.zh: 昔時運道深通，運丁或藉來往攜貨售賣以贍用；

translations.literal: Formerly the transport route was deeply navigable, and transport workers could rely on carrying goods back and forth for sale to support themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the canal ran deep and transport workers could carry goods on return trips to support themselves;

sentences.zh: 後因黃河屢經倒灌，運道受害，慮其船重難行，嚴禁多帶貨物。

translations.literal: later because the Yellow River repeatedly backed up and flooded, the transport route suffered damage; fearing boats would be too heavy to travel, carrying much cargo was strictly forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: later repeated Yellow River flooding damaged the route; fearing overloaded boats, officials strictly limited cargo.

sentences.zh: 又從前回空帶鹽，不甚搜查；

translations.literal: Moreover, formerly on empty return trips they carried salt and were not much searched;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly on empty return voyages they carried salt with little interference;

sentences.zh: 近因鹽商力絀，未免算及瑣屑，而各丁出息遂盡。

translations.literal: recently because salt merchants were strained, trifling matters were inevitably reckoned against them, and each worker's income was thus exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: recently, with salt merchants under pressure, even minor infractions were pursued, exhausting workers' supplementary income.

sentences.zh: 加以運道日淺，反多添夫撥淺之費。

translations.literal: Added to this, as the transport route grows shallower daily, there are instead more expenses for hiring laborers to pole through shallows.
translations.idiomatic: As the canal grows shallower, extra costs for hiring laborers to pole through shallows have mounted.

sentences.zh: 此費不出之州縣，更無所出。

translations.literal: If this expense does not come from the counties and districts, there is nowhere else it can come from.
translations.idiomatic: If counties and districts do not pay these costs, there is nowhere else the money can come from.

sentences.zh: 此又運丁不能上達之實情也。

translations.literal: This is again the true situation of transport workers that cannot reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: This, too, is the reality transport workers cannot convey to the throne.

sentences.zh: 數年前因津貼日增，於是定例只准給三百兩。

translations.literal: Several years ago because subsidies grew daily, a regulation was fixed allowing only three hundred taels.
translations.idiomatic: Several years ago, as subsidies mounted, regulations capped payments at three hundred taels.

sentences.zh: 運丁實不濟用，則重船不能開，州縣必獲咎戾，不免私自增給，是所謂三百兩者虛名耳。

translations.literal: Transport workers in truth cannot make ends meet; then heavy boats cannot depart and counties and districts are sure to incur blame, so they cannot but privately add more—the so-called three hundred taels is but an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred taels is insufficient; heavy boats cannot sail and magistrates face blame, so they privately add more—the regulated amount is merely nominal.

sentences.zh: 頃又以浮收過甚，嚴禁收漕不得過八折。

translations.literal: Recently because illicit surcharges were excessive, it was strictly forbidden to collect grain transport tax at more than eight-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, because surcharges had grown excessive, collection was strictly capped at eighty percent.

sentences.zh: 州縣入不敷出，則強者不敢與較，弱者仍肆朘削，是所謂八折者亦虛名耳。

translations.literal: When counties and districts have income insufficient for expenditure, the strong dare not dispute while the weak are still wantonly exploited—the so-called eight-tenths is also but an empty name.
translations.idiomatic: With magistrates' income falling short, the powerful dare not protest while the weak are still exploited—the eighty-percent cap is also merely nominal.

sentences.zh: 然民間執詞抗官，官必設法箝制，而事端因以滋生，皆出於民心之不服。

translations.literal: Yet when the people cling to arguments to resist officials, officials must devise means to restrain them, and incidents thus arise—all stemming from popular hearts' discontent.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners resist with legal arguments, officials devise means to suppress them, breeding further incidents—all stemming from popular discontent.

sentences.zh: 若將此不靖之民盡法懲處，則既困浮收，复陷法網，民心恐愈不平。

translations.literal: If these unruly commoners are all punished to the full extent of the law, they are already distressed by illicit surcharge and again fall into the legal net—popular hearts will likely grow still more discontent.
translations.idiomatic: If all such restless commoners are punished to the full extent of the law, they will be squeezed by surcharges and trapped in the legal net—popular resentment will only deepen.

sentences.zh: 若一味姑容隱忍，則小民開犯上之風，將致不必收漕，而亦目無官長。

translations.literal: If one indulges and tolerates without end, the common people will open a trend of defying superiors, leading to a state where grain transport need not be collected yet officials are also held in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: If officials indulge them endlessly, commoners will learn defiance, until grain transport is refused altogether and magistrates are held in contempt.

sentences.zh: 其於紀綱法度，所關實為匪細。

translations.literal: As for discipline and law, what is involved is truly no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: The stakes for law and order are by no means small.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下部議。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the ministry deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the relevant ministries for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 時在廷諸臣多以為言，文田持議切中時弊，最得其平。

translations.literal: At the time many court ministers had spoken on the matter; Wentian's position struck at the abuses of the age and was most even-handed.
translations.idiomatic: Many court ministers had already spoken on the matter; Wentian's analysis struck at the heart of contemporary abuses and was judged the most balanced.

sentences.zh: 詔禁浮收，裁革運丁陋規，八折之議遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict forbade illicit surcharges and cut away the transport workers' improper practices; the eight-tenths proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict banned illicit surcharges and abolished transport workers' improper practices; the eighty-percent proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 四年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1824 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In 1827 he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，依尚書例賜卹，諡文僖。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; according to the precedent for ministers, funeral favors were granted and he was given the posthumous title Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; funeral honors were granted according to ministerial precedent, and he was posthumously titled Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 文田持己方嚴，數督學政，革除陋例，斥偽體，拔真才，典試號得士。

translations.literal: Wentian held himself with strict integrity; he several times supervised education, abolished improper practices, rejected spurious literary styles, selected true talent, and when presiding over examinations was famed for obtaining worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Wentian was known for strict personal integrity; as education commissioner he abolished corrupt practices, rejected spurious examination styles, and selected genuine talent—his examinations were famed for producing worthy scholars.

sentences.zh: 論學尊宋儒，所著書則宗漢學。

translations.literal: In discussing learning he honored Song Neo-Confucians, yet in his writings he followed Han Learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his teaching he honored Song Neo-Confucianism, yet his scholarly writings followed the Han Learning tradition.

sentences.zh: 博綜群籍，兼諳天文佔驗。

translations.literal: He broadly mastered many texts and was also versed in astronomy and divination.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered a wide range of texts and was also versed in astronomy and astrological divination.

sentences.zh: 林清之變未起，彗入紫微垣；

translations.literal: Before the Lin Qing incident arose, a comet entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Lin Qing rebellion, a comet entered the Purple Forbidden Enclosure;

sentences.zh: 道光初，彗見南斗下，主外夷兵事：文田皆先事言之。

translations.literal: at the beginning of Daoguang a comet appeared below the Southern Dipper, presaging military affairs with foreign barbarians—Wentian had spoken of all these beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: at the start of the Daoguang reign a comet appeared below the Southern Dipper, portending war with foreigners—Wentian had predicted each of these events in advance.

sentences.zh: =戴敦元=戴敦元，字金溪，浙江開化人。

translations.literal: Dai Dunyuan, courtesy name Jinxi, was a native of Kaihua in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Dunyuan, whose courtesy name was Jinxi, came from Kaihua in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼有異禀，過外家，一月盡讀其室中書。

translations.literal: As a child he had an unusual gift; visiting his maternal relatives' home, in one month he read all the books in their room.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he showed unusual gifts; visiting his maternal relatives, he read every book in their house within a month.

sentences.zh: 十歲舉神童，學政彭元瑞試以文，如老宿；

translations.literal: At age ten he was nominated as a child prodigy; Education Commissioner Peng Yuanrui tested him with an essay, and it was like that of a seasoned scholar;
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was nominated as a child prodigy; when Education Commissioner Peng Yuanrui tested his essay, it read like the work of a seasoned scholar;

sentences.zh: 面問經義，答如流。

translations.literal: when questioned face to face on the meaning of the classics, he answered fluently.
translations.idiomatic: when questioned orally on classical interpretation, he answered without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「子異日必為國器！

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "You will surely become a pillar of the state in days to come!
translations.idiomatic: He exclaimed, "You will surely become a pillar of the state one day!

sentences.zh: 」年十五，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: " At age fifteen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: " At fifteen he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，散館改禮部主事，銓授刑部主事，典山西鄉試。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, and after leaving the Hanlin Academy was transferred to a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites, then appointed by selection as principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, and presided over the Shanxi provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he took the jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy, and after completing his training served as a principal clerk in the Ministries of Rites and Punishments in turn, and presided over the Shanxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to the rank of director.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十四年，出為廣東高廉道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Jiaqing he went out to serve as Intendant of Gaolian Circuit in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1819 he was posted as Intendant of the Gaolian Circuit in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢江西按察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was promoted to Provincial Judicial Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was promoted to Provincial Judicial Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 敦元初外任，以情形非素習，蘇州多粵商，過訪風土利弊，久之始去，盡得要領。

translations.literal: When Dunyuan first took an outside post, because conditions were not what he was accustomed to and Suzhou had many Cantonese merchants, he stopped to inquire about local customs and advantages and disadvantages, and only after a long while departed, having fully grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: On his first provincial posting, unfamiliar with local conditions, he stopped in Suzhou—home to many Cantonese merchants—to study regional customs and administrative problems at length before departing, having mastered the essentials.

sentences.zh: 至江西，無幕客，延屬吏諳刑名者以助，數月清積牘四千餘事。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Jiangxi, he had no private secretaries and engaged subordinate officials versed in penal matters to assist; in several months he cleared more than four thousand accumulated cases.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi he employed no private secretaries but enlisted subordinates skilled in penal law; within months he cleared more than four thousand backlogged cases.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷山西布政使，單車之任，輿夫館人莫知為達官。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi; traveling alone to his post, cart drivers and innkeepers did not know he was a high official.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was transferred to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi, traveling alone to his post so that carriers and innkeepers never guessed he was a high official.

sentences.zh: 籓署有陋規曰釐頭銀，上下取給，敦元革之，曰：「官有養廉，僕禦官所豢，何贏餘之有？

translations.literal: The provincial administration office had an improper practice called 'fraction-head silver,' taken by superiors and subordinates alike for support; Dunyuan abolished it, saying: "Officials have integrity-nurturing allowances; servants are kept by officials—what surplus profit could there be?
translations.idiomatic: The provincial office had a corrupt practice called 'fraction-head silver' skimmed at every level; Dunyuan abolished it, saying, "Officials receive integrity allowances; servants are maintained by their masters—what surplus could there be?

sentences.zh: 」調湖南，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Hunan and acted as Governor.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Hunan and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 三年，召授刑部侍郎，自此歷十年，未遷他部，專治刑獄，剖析律意，於條例有罅漏，及因時制宜者，數奏請更定。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Punishments; from then for ten years he was not transferred to another ministry, specializing in penal affairs, analyzing the intent of statutes, and where regulations had gaps or required adaptation to the times, repeatedly memorializing to request revision.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 he was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Punishments; for the next ten years he remained in that ministry, specializing in penal law, analyzing statutory intent, and repeatedly memorializing to revise regulations where gaps existed or circumstances required adaptation.

sentences.zh: 每日部事畢，歸坐一室，謝絕賓客。

translations.literal: Each day when ministry business was finished, he returned to sit alone in one room and declined visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Each day after ministry business he retired to a single room and refused visitors.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢刑部尚書，典會試。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Minister of Punishments and presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832 he was promoted to Minister of Punishments and served as chief examiner for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒，優詔賜卹，稱其清介自持，克盡職守，贈太子太保，諡簡恪。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died; a favorable edict granted funeral favors, praising his integrity and self-restraint and full discharge of duty; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the title Jianke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1834; the throne granted funeral honors, praising his integrity and dedication; he was posthumously titled Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name Jianke.

sentences.zh: 敦元博聞強識，目近視，觀書與面相磨，過輒不忘。

translations.literal: Dunyuan was broadly learned with a powerful memory; his eyes were nearsighted, and he read with his face nearly touching the book—once past, he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyuan was prodigiously learned with an extraordinary memory; nearsighted, he read with his face nearly touching the page and never forgot what he had read.

sentences.zh: 每至一官，積牘覽一過，他日吏偶誤，輒摘正之，無敢欺者。

translations.literal: Whenever he arrived at a post, he read through accumulated documents once; later if a clerk erred even slightly, he would immediately point out and correct it—none dared deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: At every post he read through the backlog once; if a clerk erred later, he corrected it immediately—no one dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 奏對有所諮詢，援引律例，誦故牘一字無舛誤，宣宗深重之。

translations.literal: When questioned in audience memorials, he cited statutes and regulations and recited old documents without a single character's error—the Xuanzong Emperor valued him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When questioned in audience, he cited statutes and recited archival documents without a single error—the Daoguang Emperor valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 至老，或問僻事；

translations.literal: In old age, if asked about obscure matters;
translations.idiomatic: In old age, when asked obscure questions;

sentences.zh: 指某書某卷，百不一爽。

translations.literal: he would point to such-and-such book and volume, never once mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: he would cite the exact book and volume without ever being wrong.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「書籍浩如煙海，人生豈能盡閱？

translations.literal: He once said: "Books are vast as a smoke-filled sea—how can one person in a lifetime read them all?
translations.idiomatic: He once remarked, "Books are vast as the sea—how can one person read them all in a lifetime?

sentences.zh: 天下惟此義理，古今人所談，往往雷同。

translations.literal: Under heaven there is only this principle; what people ancient and modern discuss is often the same.
translations.idiomatic: Under heaven there is only this body of principle; what thinkers ancient and modern discuss is often the same.

sentences.zh: 當世以為獨得者，大抵昔人唾餘。

translations.literal: What the present age considers uniquely obtained is mostly what men of old spat out as leftovers.
translations.idiomatic: What the present age treats as original insight is mostly what earlier thinkers had already discarded.

sentences.zh: 」罕自為文，僅傳詩數卷。

translations.literal: " He rarely wrote on his own; only a few volumes of poetry survive.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote little himself; only a few volumes of poetry survive.

sentences.zh: 喜天文、律算，討論有年，亦未自立一說。

translations.literal: He delighted in astronomy and mathematical harmonics, discussed them for years, yet never established a theory of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in astronomy and mathematics and discussed them for years, yet never developed a theory of his own.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，笥無餘衣，囷無餘粟，庀其貲不​​及百金，廉潔蓋性成雲。

translations.literal: On the day of his death his chest held no spare clothes, his granary no spare grain; arranging his estate did not reach one hundred taels—integrity and frugality were perhaps inborn.
translations.idiomatic: At his death his chest held no spare clothes and his granary no spare grain; his estate amounted to less than one hundred taels—integrity and frugality were evidently inborn.

sentences.zh: =朱士彥=朱士彥，字修承，江蘇寶應人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shiyan, courtesy name Xiucheng, was a native of Baoying in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shiyan, whose courtesy name was Xiucheng, came from Baoying in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父彬，績學通經，見儒林傳。

translations.literal: His father Bin was a scholar of solid learning versed in the classics; see the Biographies of Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bin was a distinguished classical scholar; see his biography in the Confucian Scholars section.

sentences.zh: 士彥承家學。

translations.literal: Shiyan inherited the family learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan inherited his family's scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 成嘉慶七年一甲三名進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi of the third rank in the first class and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he took the jinshi degree as third in the first class and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 纂國史河渠志，諳習河事。

translations.literal: He compiled the River Control section of the National History and became thoroughly versed in river affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled the river-control section of the National History and became thoroughly versed in hydraulic engineering.

sentences.zh: 大考擢贊善，督湖北學政。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he was promoted to Tutor and supervised education in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand examination he was promoted to tutor and appointed education commissioner for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍讀學士，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Reader and entered service in the Upper Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Reader and was assigned to the Upper Study.

sentences.zh: 歷少詹事、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served successively as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he was promoted to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，以南河高堰壞，疏陳河工事宜，論：「高堰石工宜切實估修；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because the Gaoyan dam on the Southern River was damaged, he submitted a memorial on river works affairs, arguing: "The stone works of Gaoyan dam should be genuinely estimated and repaired;
translations.idiomatic: In 1824, after the Gaoyan dam on the Southern River failed, he memorialized on river works, arguing: "The stone works at Gaoyan must be honestly assessed and repaired;

sentences.zh: 堰內二堤宜培補；

translations.literal: the two inner embankments of the dam should be reinforced;
translations.idiomatic: the two inner embankments should be reinforced;

sentences.zh: 黃河盛漲，宜兩岸分洩；

translations.literal: when the Yellow River floods heavily, both banks should discharge in division;
translations.idiomatic: when the Yellow River floods heavily, both banks should be used for controlled discharge;

sentences.zh: 山盱五壩宜相機開放；

translations.literal: the five dams of Shanxu should be opened as circumstances permit;
translations.idiomatic: the five Shanxu dams should be opened as circumstances require;

sentences.zh: 黃河下游無堤之處宜接築。

translations.literal: where the lower Yellow River has no dikes, dikes should be joined and built."
translations.idiomatic: unembanked sections of the lower Yellow River should receive connecting dikes."

sentences.zh: 」下勘河大臣文孚籌議酌行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to River Investigation Commissioner Wen Fu to deliberate and implement as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to River Investigation Commissioner Wen Fu for deliberation and selective implementation.

sentences.zh: 尋督浙江學政。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he supervised education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed education commissioner for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 奏禁諸生包漕鬧漕，以端士習。

translations.literal: He memorialized prohibiting degree candidates from monopolizing grain transport and disrupting it, to rectify scholarly conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to prohibit students from monopolizing and disrupting grain transport, to restore proper scholarly conduct.

sentences.zh: 御史錢儀吉劾士彥任性，詔嘉士彥能任勞怨；

translations.literal: Censor Qian Yiji impeached Shiyan for willfulness; an edict praised Shiyan for being able to bear labor and resentment;
translations.idiomatic: Censor Qian Yiji impeached Shiyan for willfulness; the throne praised Shiyan for willingness to bear hardship and resentment;

sentences.zh: 惟斥其父彬就養閱卷，及命題割裂，薄譴之。

translations.literal: only rebuking his father Bin for receiving support while grading examination papers and for fragmenting examination topics, with a light reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: but lightly reprimanded his father Bin for grading papers while receiving support from his son and for fragmenting examination topics.

sentences.zh: 九年，典會試，督安徽學政，尋擢左都御史，召還京。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he presided over the metropolitan examination, supervised education in Anhui, was soon promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1829 he presided over the metropolitan examination and supervised education in Anhui, was soon promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief, and recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1831 he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 是秋，江蘇大水，河、淮、湖同時漲溢，命偕尚書穆彰阿往勘。

translations.literal: That autumn Jiangsu suffered great flooding; the rivers, Huai, and lakes all rose and overflowed simultaneously; he was ordered to go with Minister Mujang'a to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn catastrophic flooding struck Jiangsu as the Yellow River, Huai, and lakes overflowed together; he was ordered to investigate alongside Minister Mujang'a.

sentences.zh: 穆彰阿先回京，遂偕左都御史白鎔察視江蘇、安徽水災賑務。

translations.literal: Mujang'a returned to the capital first; he then accompanied Left Censor-in-Chief Bai Rong to inspect flood disaster relief in Jiangsu and Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: After Mujang'a returned to the capital, he accompanied Left Censor-in-Chief Bai Rong to oversee flood relief in Jiangsu and Anhui.

sentences.zh: 疏言：揚河廳掣卸石工，及纖堤耳閘，應令工員賠修；

translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that stone works torn away at the Yanghe Bureau and the slender embankment ear sluice should be repaired at engineering officers' expense;

translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Huai–Yang local officials were often acting appointees unfamiliar with conditions, and requested that Jiangning Administration Commissioner Lin Zexu and Circuit Intendant Zhang Yuesong oversee northern Jiangsu relief—the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 尋奏：「續查下河積潦之區，被災尤重，浮開戶口，為辦賑積弊。

translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized: "Further investigation of the lower-river flood zones found especially severe damage; inflating household registers is a longstanding abuse in relief administration.

translations.literal: Commissioners should be ordered to investigate and then immediately post lists in the native township; when distributing relief, county and district magistrates should issue relief according to one consolidated list from the commissioners' original investigation, with chief investigators conducting spot checks for verification.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners should investigate and post verified lists in each township; magistrates should distribute relief from a single consolidated register, with chief investigators conducting spot checks for verification.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「山盱廳屬添建滾水石壩，本年啟放過水，現已無從查驗。

translations.idiomatic: " He also reported: "The newly built overflow stone dam in Shanxu jurisdiction was opened this year and can no longer be inspected while water remains high.

translations.idiomatic: Engineering officers reported cracks in the stone base and damage to the lime and earth below when the dam was opened; repairs should be required once water levels fall.

sentences.zh: 堰、盱兩廳淮、湖石工掣卸二百餘丈，固限未滿，應令賠修。

translations.literal: At the Yan and Xu bureaus, Huai and lake stone works torn away exceed two hundred zhang; the warranty period is not yet fulfilled—they should be ordered to repair at their own expense.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yan and Xu bureaus, over two hundred zhang of Huai and lake stone works were torn away before their warranty expired—engineering officers should repair them at their own expense.

sentences.zh: 其石後磚工灰工間有殘缺，應令補築。

translations.literal: Behind the stone, brick and lime works have gaps in places—they should be ordered supplemented and built.
translations.idiomatic: Brick and lime work behind the stone has gaps in places and should be repaired.

sentences.zh: 又盱堰大堤，加幫土工間有蟄低浮松之處，應培補，責成河兵種柳護堤。

translations.literal: Moreover, on the Xuyan great embankment, where additional earth was piled, there are places sunk low and loosely floating—they should be reinforced, with river soldiers charged to plant willows to protect the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: On the Xuyan great embankment, reinforced earthwork has sunk and loosened in places and should be rebuilt, with river soldiers assigned to plant willows for protection.

sentences.zh: 其已估未辦之高堰頭、二兩堡，未估之智、信兩壩，應即興辦。

translations.literal: The Gaoyan head and second and third forts already estimated but not yet undertaken, and the Zhi and Xin dams not yet estimated, should be immediately undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoyan head fort and second and third forts, already estimated but not started, and the Zhi and Xin dams, not yet estimated, should be undertaken immediately.

sentences.zh: 此項與黃河險要不同，向來保固一年。

translations.idiomatic: Unlike critical Yellow River sections, these works have traditionally carried a one-year warranty.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後各廳土堤及運河堤岸，均改保固三年。

translations.idiomatic: He requested that earthen embankments at all bureaus and Grand Canal banks hereafter carry a three-year warranty.

sentences.zh: 運河埽工於經歷一年後，再加保固二年，驗明堅整，始準埽汛修防。

translations.literal: For Grand Canal revetment works, after one year has passed, add two more years of warranty; once verified solid and intact, only then permit revetment-flood-season repair and defense.
translations.idiomatic: For canal revetment works, after one year an additional two-year warranty should apply; only after verification of sound construction should they enter routine flood-season maintenance.

sentences.zh: 」「安徽無為州江壩及銅陵縣壩工程緊要，均應藉款興修。

translations.idiomatic: " The Jiang dam at Wuwei in Anhui and the Tongling County dam are critical projects and should both be funded and undertaken.

sentences.zh: 」並下所司議行。

translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.

translations.literal: He also impeached Yancheng, Susong, Qingyang, and other counties for delayed and incomplete disaster reporting, requesting punishment;
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Yancheng, Susong, Qingyang, and other counties for delayed and incomplete disaster reports, requesting punishment;

sentences.zh: 捐賑紳民應給議敘；

translations.literal: gentry and commoners who donated for relief should be given consideration for honors;
translations.idiomatic: gentry who donated to relief efforts should receive honors;

sentences.zh: 禁胥吏婪索挑剔：並從之。

translations.literal: prohibiting clerks and runners from greedy extortion and nitpicking—all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: and prohibiting clerks from extortion and petty harassment—all was approved.

sentences.zh: 十二年，事竣回京。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when affairs were concluded, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1832, when his mission was complete, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 南河於家灣奸民陳端等盜挖官堤，掣動河流，复偕穆彰阿往勘。

translations.idiomatic: At Yujiawan on the Southern River, scoundrels led by Chen Duan illicitly dug the official embankment and diverted the current; he again accompanied Mujang'a to investigate.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「九月初旬，清口出水二尺有餘，高堰長水二丈一尺，勢至危險。

translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "In early September, Qingkou discharged over two chi of water and Gaoyan stood at two zhang one chi—the situation was extremely dangerous.

translations.idiomatic: At that time the seven Wucheng forts had not yet been opened, and Hong Lake bore the full pressure.

translations.literal: Now they have been opened and lake water has been reduced.
translations.idiomatic: They have now been opened and lake levels have fallen.

translations.literal: Winter is now at hand; after one month work will be difficult to undertake; the lakes hold much accumulated water and fierce winds are to be feared—urgent completion is requested.
translations.idiomatic: Winter is approaching; within a month construction will become impossible; lakes still hold much water and fierce winds are a concern—urgent completion is requested.

sentences.zh: 」尋命复偕侍郎敬徵往勘。

translations.idiomatic: " He was soon ordered to investigate again alongside Vice Minister Jingzheng.

translations.idiomatic: In 1833 he reported that although the main Yujiawan dam had been closed, additional reinforcement and compaction should be ordered to prevent failure.

sentences.zh: 覆訊挖堤諸犯，治如律。

translations.literal: He re-examined the offenders who dug the embankment and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He re-examined the embankment-digging offenders and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 又偕敬徵覆勘河、湖各工，請分別緩急，以次辦理。

translations.literal: He again accompanied Jingzheng in re-investigating river and lake works, requesting that urgency and delay be distinguished and matters handled in order.
translations.idiomatic: He again accompanied Jingzheng to re-inspect river and lake works, requesting that projects be prioritized and handled in sequence.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he returned home for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 十六年，服闋，署吏部尚書，偕尚書耆英赴廣東、江西鞫獄。

translations.idiomatic: In 1836, after mourning ended, he served as acting Minister of Personnel and accompanied Minister Qiying to Guangdong and Jiangxi to adjudicate cases.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 查勘浙江海塘，遂赴南河驗料垛工程，盤查倉庫。

translations.idiomatic: He inspected the Zhejiang seawall, then went to the Southern River to verify material-stockpile projects and audited warehouses.

translations.idiomatic: Finding warehouse stock did not match the records, he impeached River Warehouse Intendant Li Xiangzhi and stripped him of office.

translations.idiomatic: He also investigated affairs in Anhui and Henan and memorialized on Ever-Normal Granary regulations: "Each province should cover prisoner grain and relay transport from regular expenditures without drawing on Ever-Normal reserves;

translations.idiomatic: fair-price sales should be permitted only when market prices exceed eight qian;

translations.literal: purchase must wait until years of abundance when grain is cheap, and must be two or three years after sale, to ease the people's strength and remove longstanding abuses."
translations.idiomatic: purchases should wait until years of abundance when grain is cheap, and should occur only two or three years after sales, to ease the people's burden and remove longstanding abuses."

sentences.zh: 如議行。

translations.literal: As deliberated, it was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals were adopted and implemented.

sentences.zh: 十八年，兼管順天府尹事，典會試。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he concurrently managed the affairs of the Shuntian Prefect and presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1838 he concurrently served as Shuntian Prefect and presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 士彥以綜覈為宣宗所知，奉使按事皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Shiyan was known to the Xuanzong Emperor for his comprehensive scrutiny; on missions to investigate affairs he always met with imperial approval.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan was known to the Daoguang Emperor for his thoroughness; on investigative missions he always met with imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，詔嘉其性情直爽，辦事公正，贈太子太保，賜其四子舉人、副榜貢生有差，諡文定。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; an edict praised his straightforward character and fair handling of affairs; he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his four sons were granted juren, supplementary-list tribute students, and other honors in varying degrees; he was posthumously titled Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after; the throne praised his straightforward character and fair judgment; he was posthumously titled Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his four sons received juren degrees and other honors; his posthumous name was Wending.

translations.idiomatic: He Linghan, whose courtesy name was Xiancha, came from Daozhou in Hunan.

translations.idiomatic: As a selected tribute student, he passed examination and was appointed a seventh-rank clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi of the third rank in the first class and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he took the jinshi degree as third in the first class and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢司業。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he placed second class and was promoted to Vice Director of Studies.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand examination he placed second class and was promoted to Vice Director of Studies.

sentences.zh: 累遷右庶子。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Right Vice President of the Supervisorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice President of the Supervisorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 典廣東、福建鄉試，留福建學政。

translations.literal: He presided over the provincial examinations of Guangdong and Fujian and remained as education commissioner in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Guangdong and Fujian provincial examinations and remained as education commissioner in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 令諸生自註誦習何經，據以考校，所取拔貢多樸學。

translations.literal: He ordered students to note for themselves which classic they recited and studied, and examined them accordingly; those he selected as tribute students were mostly solid scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He required students to record which classic they studied and examined them accordingly; most of those he selected as tribute students were solid scholars of genuine learning.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，授順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he was appointed Shuntian Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was appointed Shuntian Prefect.

sentences.zh: 京畿獄訟繁多，自立簿籍，每月按簿催結，無留獄。

translations.literal: Prison lawsuits in the capital region were numerous; he established his own register and each month pressed for closure according to the register, with no cases left in detention.
translations.idiomatic: With lawsuits flooding the capital region, he kept his own register and pressed monthly for closures, leaving no cases in detention.

sentences.zh: 遷大理寺卿，仍署府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to President of the Court of Judicial Review while still acting as Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to President of the Court of Judicial Review while continuing to act as Shuntian Prefect.

sentences.zh: 在任凡五年，歷左副都御史、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In office altogether five years, he served successively as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Over five years in office he served as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief and Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 典浙江鄉試，留學政。

translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Zhejiang provincial examination and remained as education commissioner.

translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Governor-General Cheng Zuluo to investigate collusion and fraud among gentry, secretaries, and clerks in Shanyin and Kuaiji, he established the facts, secured the dismissal of Acting Provincial Judicial Commissioner Li Yun, and secured varying punishments for other offenders.

translations.idiomatic: Before his term ended he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, recalled to the capital, and again placed in charge of Shuntian Prefect affairs.

translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Revenue, then back to Personnel, while still acting as Vice Minister of Revenue.

translations.idiomatic: Censor Nasihong'a proposed barring promotion for local officials with grain-tax penalties and reforming miscellaneous taxes; the matter was referred to the ministries.

translations.literal: Linghan held concurrent charge of the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue and rejected it, saying: "Managing complex and urgent affairs is always hard to find the right person for; if barred by penalties incurred in official business, one will end up promoting and transferring only mediocre men without fault.
translations.idiomatic: Linghan, holding concurrent charge of Personnel and Revenue, rejected the proposal: "Managing difficult posts requires exceptional talent; barring officials with routine penalties would leave only mediocre, faultless candidates for promotion.

translations.idiomatic: If every prefecture and county nationwide imposes such taxes, merchants will raise prices on daily necessities and pass costs to the people; officials will extract transport and conversion charges as well;

translations.literal: moreover businesses open and close unpredictably, tax amounts are hard to fix—there is a name for collecting resentment but no reality of enriching the state.

translations.idiomatic: In 1834 he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and appointed Minister of Works while continuing to manage the Prefect's office.
