translations.literal: He repeatedly acted as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十七年，吏部因京察一等人員有先由御史改官者議駁。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Ministry of Personnel rejected first-class personnel in the capital inspection who had previously been censors transferred to other posts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1837 the Ministry of Personnel rejected first-class capital-inspection candidates who had previously transferred from the censorate.

sentences.zh: 凌漢以不勝御史，非不勝外任者比，如此苛繩，有妨言路。

translations.literal: Linghan argued that failure as a censor is not comparable to failure in outside appointment; such harsh binding harms the avenue of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Linghan argued that failure as a censor differs from failure in provincial service; such harsh restrictions would obstruct the remonstrance system.

sentences.zh: 御史改部之員，例準截取。

translations.literal: Those who transferred from the censorate to ministries are by precedent permitted selection.
translations.idiomatic: Censors transferred to ministries are by precedent eligible for selection.

sentences.zh: 至京察雖無明文，從前有御史降調保送員外郎者，援以請旨。

translations.literal: As for capital inspection, though there is no explicit text, formerly there were censors demoted and transferred who were nominated as department directors—he cited this to request imperial decision.
translations.idiomatic: Though capital inspection had no explicit rule, he cited precedent of demoted censors nominated as department directors and requested an imperial ruling.

sentences.zh: 因面奏現任大員花傑、吳榮光，皆曾由御史改降，遂奏俞允。

translations.literal: He cited in audience the current high officials Hua Jie and Wu Rongguang, both of whom had been demoted after transferring from the censorate; the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Citing in audience current high officials Hua Jie and Wu Rongguang, both demoted former censors, he secured imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 十九年，調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 四川總督寶興請按糧津貼防邊經費，議駁之，略謂：「川省地丁額徵六十六萬，田賦之輕，甲於天下。

translations.literal: Sichuan Governor-General Bao Xing requested a grain surcharge for frontier defense funds; he rejected it in deliberation, stating in summary: "Sichuan's land-poll and labor-service levy totals 660,000 taels; its land tax is the lightest in the empire.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan Governor-General Bao Xing proposed a grain surcharge for frontier defense, Linghan rejected it: "Sichuan's land tax totals 660,000 taels—the lightest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 現議按糧一兩加津貼二兩，百畝之家，不過出銀三兩，即得百萬兩，小民未必即苦輸將。

translations.literal: The present proposal adds two taels subsidy per tael of grain tax; a household of one hundred mu would pay no more than three taels of silver and one million taels would be obtained—the common people may not immediately suffer in paying.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal adds two taels per tael of tax; a hundred-mu household would pay only three taels, yielding one million taels—commoners might not feel immediate hardship.

sentences.zh: 然較原課幾增兩倍，非藏富於民之義，軍需藉資民力，尤不可率以為常。

translations.literal: Yet compared with the original levy it nearly doubles—not in the spirit of storing wealth among the people; military needs drawing on popular strength especially cannot be made routine.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it nearly doubles the original levy—contrary to storing wealth among the people—and military funding drawn from popular strength must not become routine.

sentences.zh: 請於各省秋撥項下借撥百萬兩，以三十萬為初設邊防經費，餘或發商，或置田，所獲息以四萬為常年經費，二萬提還借款，於防邊恤民兩有裨益。

translations.literal: It is requested to borrow one million taels from each province's autumn disbursement items: 300,000 for initial frontier defense funds, the remainder lent to merchants or invested in land; interest obtained—40,000 for annual funds, 20,000 to repay the loan—benefits both frontier defense and care for the people.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed borrowing one million taels from provincial autumn disbursements: 300,000 for initial frontier defense, the rest lent or invested in land; annual interest of 40,000 would fund operations and 20,000 repay the loan—benefiting both frontier defense and the people.

sentences.zh: 」詔允行。

translations.literal: " An edict approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 是年，典順天鄉試。

translations.literal: That year he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: That year he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 子紹基亦典試福建，父子同持文柄，時人榮之。

translations.literal: His son Shaoji also presided over the examination in Fujian; father and son together held literary authority, and people of the time took it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaoji also presided over the Fujian examination; father and son holding examination authority together was celebrated at the time.

sentences.zh: 二十年，卒，贈太子太保，諡文安。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he died; he was given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and posthumously titled Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1840 and was posthumously titled Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the name Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 紹基官編修，見文苑傳。

translations.literal: Shaoji served as Hanlin Compiler; see the Biographies of Literary Men.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoji served as a Hanlin compiler; see his biography in the Literary Men section.

sentences.zh: =李振祜=李振祜，字錫名，安徽太湖人。

translations.literal: Li Zhenhu, courtesy name Ximing, was a native of Taihu in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhenhu, whose courtesy name was Ximing, came from Taihu in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 進士，嘉慶六年進士，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing and was appointed Inner Cabinet Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1801 he took the jinshi degree and was appointed an Inner Cabinet secretary.

sentences.zh: 典廣西、雲南鄉試，遷宗人府主事。

translations.literal: He presided over the provincial examinations of Guangxi and Yunnan and was transferred to a director in the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Guangxi and Yunnan provincial examinations and was transferred to a director in the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 調兵部，遷員外郎，典陝甘鄉試，改御史、給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of War, promoted to Department Director, presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination, and was changed to Censor and Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministry of War, rose to department director, presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination, and was appointed censor and supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 巡視淮安漕務，劾戶部郎中錢學彬係不勝外任之員，違例截取知府，詔譴吏、戶二部堂官，予振祜議敘；

translations.literal: Inspecting Huai'an grain transport affairs, he impeached Revenue Department Director Qian Xuebin as unfit for outside appointment yet irregularly selected as prefect; an edict rebuked the chief officials of the Ministries of Personnel and Revenue and granted Zhenhu honors consideration;
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Huai'an grain transport, he impeached Revenue Director Qian Xuebin as unfit for provincial service yet irregularly selected as prefect; the throne rebuked Personnel and Revenue ministers and honored Zhenhu;

sentences.zh: 又劾都察院京察給事中色成額先經列入六法，自赴公堂辯論，干求改列三等，反覆視若兒戲，都御史被嚴議，色成額仍列有疾。

translations.literal: He also impeached Censorate capital-inspection Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, who had first been listed among the six punishments yet came in person to the public hall to argue, seeking to be changed to third class, treating the matter back and forth like child's play; the Censor-in-Chief was severely deliberated upon, yet Se Cheng'e was still listed as having illness.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Supervising Secretary Se Cheng'e, listed for severe punishment in capital inspection yet who argued in person to be downgraded to third class, treating the process as a game; the Censor-in-Chief was severely censured while Se Cheng'e was listed merely as ill.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣侍讀學士，督山東學政。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Attendant Reader of the Inner Cabinet and supervised education in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant Reader of the Inner Cabinet and was appointed education commissioner for Shandong.

sentences.zh: 應詔密陳山東積弊四事，略曰：「吏事叢脞，莫甚於官民不相安也。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he confidentially memorialized four accumulated abuses in Shandong, stating in summary: "Official affairs are tangled and complex—nothing exceeds the lack of peace between officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he confidentially memorialized four longstanding abuses in Shandong: "Official business is hopelessly tangled—nothing exceeds the estrangement between officials and people.

sentences.zh: 詞訟之繁，始由於官吏不辦，今又變而不敢辦。

translations.literal: The proliferation of lawsuits at first stemmed from officials not handling cases; now it has changed to their not daring to handle them.
translations.idiomatic: Lawsuits proliferated first because officials failed to act; now they dare not act at all.

sentences.zh: 欲結一案，輒慮翻控；

translations.literal: wishing to close a case, they constantly fear counter-accusation;
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to close a case, they fear counter-accusation;

sentences.zh: 欲用一刑，輒慮反噬。

translations.literal: wishing to apply a punishment, they constantly fear retaliation.
translations.idiomatic: wishing to impose punishment, they fear retaliation.

sentences.zh: 鞫案之時，有倚老逞刁者，有恃婦女肆潑者，有當堂憤起者，有抗不畫供者，總由官吏恩信不結於平時，明決不著於臨事，以畏葸之才識，治刁悍之民風，殆於鑿枘不相入矣。

translations.literal: When examining cases, some rely on age to act craftily, some rely on women to behave riotously, some rise in anger in court, some resist signing confessions—all because officials do not establish favor and trust in ordinary times and do not show clarity and decisiveness when matters arise; using timid talent and judgment to govern a crafty and fierce popular custom is like square and round pegs that cannot fit.
translations.idiomatic: At trial some play on age, some deploy riotous women, some rage in court, some refuse to sign confessions—all because officials build no trust in ordinary times and show no decisiveness in crisis; timid officials governing a fierce populace is like forcing square pegs into round holes.

sentences.zh: 案牘壅滯，半由外府不辦事也。

translations.literal: Backlogged documents are half due to outer prefectures not handling affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Half the case backlog stems from prefectural governments failing to act.

sentences.zh: 各府州案件，動輒提省，委交首府，其中有不必提而輕提者，亦有各府州畏難而稟請提省者。

translations.literal: Cases from each prefecture and department are constantly transferred to the province and entrusted to the capital prefecture; among them are those unnecessarily and lightly transferred, and also those where each prefecture and department, fearing difficulty, memorializes requesting provincial transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural cases are routinely transferred to the provincial capital and entrusted to the capital prefecture—some needlessly, others because prefectures fear difficulty and request transfer.

sentences.zh: 濟南府統轄十六州縣，自治不暇，而舍己耘人，勢必兩廢。

translations.literal: Jinan Prefecture governs sixteen counties and districts and has no leisure for its own administration, yet abandons its own fields to cultivate others'—both are bound to fail.
translations.idiomatic: Jinan Prefecture governs sixteen counties yet cannot manage its own affairs while taking on others'—both must fail.

sentences.zh: 各府州畏難之事，輒以一稟提省卸責，轉得遂其取巧偷安之計。

translations.literal: Matters each prefecture and department fear are handled by one memorial transferring to the province to shed responsibility, thereby achieving their scheme of taking shortcuts and seeking ease.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures transfer difficult cases to the province with a single memorial to shed responsibility, achieving their scheme of shortcuts and ease.

sentences.zh: 且疑難案件，本地聞見較真，遠提至省，則茫無頭緒，必致訟師盤踞省城，遇事挑唆，一事株連數十人，一案壓擱一二載，是欲辦案而轉以延案，欲弭訟而適以滋訟矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, in difficult cases local knowledge is more reliable; transferred far to the province, there is no clue where to begin, inevitably causing litigation masters to occupy the provincial capital, stirring up trouble at every turn, one matter implicating dozens, one case delayed one or two years—wishing to handle cases yet prolonging them, wishing to end lawsuits yet increasing them.
translations.idiomatic: Difficult cases are better understood locally; transferred to the provincial capital, investigators lack context, litigation masters flock to the city, one case implicates dozens and stalls for years—intending to resolve cases while prolonging them, intending to reduce lawsuits while multiplying them.

sentences.zh: 緝捕無策，則盜賊充斥也。

translations.literal: With no strategy for arrest, bandits fill the land.
translations.idiomatic: Without effective arrest policy, bandits fill the land.

sentences.zh: 東省盜賊，結黨剽掠，處處有之。

translations.literal: In the eastern province bandits form gangs and plunder—everywhere there are such.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong bandits form gangs and plunder everywhere.

sentences.zh: 護贓行強，雖小竊而情同大盜；

translations.literal: protecting stolen goods and acting with force, though petty theft the circumstances equal great robbery;
translations.idiomatic: They protect stolen goods and act with force—even petty theft equals major robbery;

sentences.zh: 分肥藐法，雖士類亦甘作窩家。

translations.literal: sharing spoils and despising the law, even gentry willingly serve as receivers.
translations.idiomatic: sharing spoils and defying the law, even gentry serve as fences.

sentences.zh: 劫去馬牛，定價勒贖，明目張膽，毫不畏官。

translations.literal: Seizing horses and cattle, fixing prices and extorting ransom, openly and boldly, utterly unafraid of officials.
translations.idiomatic: They seize livestock, fix ransom prices, and act openly without fear of officials.

sentences.zh: 總緣捕役悉與勾連，平日分贓，臨時送信。

translations.literal: All because constables and runners are entirely in collusion, sharing spoils in ordinary times and sending warnings when action is taken.
translations.idiomatic: This stems from constables' collusion—sharing spoils daily and warning bandits when arrests are attempted.

sentences.zh: 甚至失事者以訴懇官捕為累，以備價私贖為便。

translations.literal: Victims even regard appealing for official arrest as a burden and paying ransom privately as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Victims even regard official prosecution as a burden and private ransom as preferable.

sentences.zh: 州縣既吝養捕之資，又不講練捕之法；

translations.literal: Counties and districts are both stingy with funds for maintaining constables and do not teach methods of training them;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates stint on constables' pay and neglect their training;

sentences.zh: 既無獲盜之賞，又不嚴通盜之誅。

translations.literal: there are neither rewards for capturing bandits nor strict punishment for harboring them.
translations.idiomatic: they offer no rewards for captures and punish collusion lightly.

sentences.zh: 兼以自顧處分，動思諱飾，化大為小，咸所不免。

translations.literal: Added to this, fearing penalties for themselves, officials constantly think to conceal, turning great into small—all cannot be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing penalties, officials constantly conceal crimes, downgrading serious cases—all inevitable.

sentences.zh: 緝捕之弊如此。

translations.literal: Such are the abuses in arrest and pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the abuses in law enforcement.

sentences.zh: 錢糧不清，則虧空難杜也。

translations.literal: When grain taxes are unclear, deficits are hard to stop.
translations.idiomatic: When tax accounts are unclear, deficits cannot be prevented.

sentences.zh: 東省州縣正雜錢糧，新舊挪掩，習為故常。

translations.literal: In the eastern province counties and districts' regular and miscellaneous grain taxes are shifted and covered between old and new—a practice habitual.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong, magistrates routinely shift and cover regular and miscellaneous tax accounts between old and new.

sentences.zh: 其弊由於交代不清，自三四任以至十餘任，轇葛不清者，比比皆是。

translations.literal: The abuse stems from unclear handovers—from three or four terms to more than ten, tangled and unclear cases are everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: The abuse stems from unclear handovers—accounts tangled across three to ten successive magistrates are everywhere.

sentences.zh: 官虧而外，更有書虧。

translations.literal: Beyond official deficits there are also clerks' deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond official deficits are clerks' deficits.

sentences.zh: 查書虧情弊，或串通幕丁，朦混本官；

translations.literal: Investigating clerks' deficit abuses, some collude with secretaries and runners to deceive their superior;
translations.idiomatic: Clerks' deficits involve collusion with secretaries to deceive magistrates;

sentences.zh: 私雕假印，偽造串票。

translations.literal: privately carving false seals and forging linked receipts.
translations.idiomatic: forging seals and receipts.

sentences.zh: 有滿其私橐而遠颺者，有挾制本官而自供不諱者。

translations.literal: Some fill their private purses and flee far away; some coerce their superior and confess without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Some fill their purses and flee; others coerce magistrates and confess openly.

sentences.zh: 州縣迴護，處分隱忍代認，而奸書遂益以侵蝕為得計。

translations.literal: Counties and districts shield them, penalties are endured and acknowledged on their behalf, and wicked clerks thus increasingly take encroachment as their strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates shield them, accepting penalties on their behalf, so wicked clerks increasingly treat embezzlement as sound policy.

sentences.zh: 錢糧之弊如此。

translations.literal: Such are the abuses in grain taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the abuses in tax collection.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was well received by the throne.

sentences.zh: 又劾泰安知府延璐、東昌知府熊方受請，飭交撫臣查察嚴參；

translations.literal: He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fang for accepting bribes, ordering the governor to investigate and impeach severely;
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Tai'an Prefect Yan Lu and Dongchang Prefect Xiong Fang for bribery, ordering the governor to investigate and impeach;

sentences.zh: 又劾東昌知府王果陵辱生員，褫王果職；

translations.literal: he also impeached Dongchang Prefect Wang Guo for insulting a degree candidate and stripped Wang Guo of office;
translations.idiomatic: he also impeached Dongchang Prefect Wang Guo for insulting a student and stripped him of office;

sentences.zh: 又察出假印試卷、勾結舞弊之人，奏請懲辦。

translations.literal: he also uncovered examination papers with false seals and persons colluding in fraud, memorializing to request punishment.
translations.idiomatic: he uncovered forged examination papers and examination fraud and memorialized for punishment.

sentences.zh: =宗室恩桂=宗室恩桂，字小山，隸鑲藍旗。

translations.literal: Zong Shi Engui, courtesy name Xiaoshan, was of the Bordered Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Engui of the Imperial Clan, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshan, belonged to the Bordered Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 道光二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1822 he took the jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 九遷至內閣學士，兼副都統。

translations.literal: Through nine promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet, concurrently serving as Vice Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Through nine promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet and Vice Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授盛京工部侍郎，尋召為兵部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Vice Minister of Works at Mukden, soon recalled as Vice Minister of War, then transferred to Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1835 he was appointed Vice Minister of Works at Mukden, soon recalled as Vice Minister of War, then transferred to Personnel.

sentences.zh: 因曠文職六班，降內閣學士。

translations.literal: Because he was absent from six sessions of civil office, he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: Absent from six civil office sessions, he was demoted to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.

sentences.zh: 歷工部、吏部侍郎，管理國子監事，兼護軍統領、左右翼總兵。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Works and Personnel, managed Imperial Academy affairs, and concurrently was Commander of the Guard, and Commander-in-Chief of the Left and Right Wings.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Minister of Works and Personnel, managed the Imperial Academy, and concurrently commanded the Guard and the Left and Right Wings.

sentences.zh: 十九年，典順天鄉試，偕大理寺卿何汝霖往浙江按學政李國杞被劾事，遂查勘南河、東河料垛，奏劾虛缺浮用者，議譴有差。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination and accompanied President of the Court of Judicial Review He Rulin to Zhejiang to investigate the impeached Education Commissioner Li Guoqi; he then inspected material stockpiles on the Southern and Eastern rivers, memorializing to impeach those with false shortages and excessive use, with varying degrees of censure deliberated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1839 he presided over the Shuntian examination and accompanied Court President He Rulin to Zhejiang to investigate Education Commissioner Li Guoqi; he then inspected Southern and Eastern River material stockpiles, impeaching those with false shortages and excessive spending, with varying punishments.

sentences.zh: 二十年，充內務府大臣，管理上駟院。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he served as Minister of the Imperial Household and managed the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In 1840 he served as Minister of the Imperial Household and managed the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 議增圓明園丁四百名，命偕尚書賽尚阿督率訓練。

translations.literal: It was proposed to add four hundred gardeners for the Old Summer Palace; he was ordered with Minister Saishanga to supervise and train them.
translations.idiomatic: When four hundred Old Summer Palace guards were added, he was ordered with Minister Saishanga to train them.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授理籓院尚書，兼署左都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and concurrently acted as Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1841 he was appointed Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs and acting Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 劾太常寺丞豐伸及查倉御史廣祜不職，並罷之。

translations.literal: He impeached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Feng Shen and granary-inspection Censor Guang Hu for dereliction of duty and dismissed both.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Sacrifices Vice Director Feng Shen and granary Censor Guang Hu for dereliction and dismissed both.

sentences.zh: 署步軍統領。

translations.literal: He acted as Commander of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Commander of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「京城巡捕五營槍兵一千名，不足以資捍衛，增設一千。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The capital's five patrol battalions have one thousand musket soldiers, insufficient for defense—add one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "The capital's five patrol battalions have only one thousand musket troops, insufficient for defense—add one thousand.

sentences.zh: 裁撤藤牌弓箭等兵，改為槍兵；

translations.literal: Abolish rattan-shield archers and similar troops and change them to musket soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Replace rattan-shield archers with musket troops;

sentences.zh: 不敷者，於各營兵丁內揀選足額。

translations.literal: where insufficient, select from soldiers in each battalion to fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: fill shortfalls by selecting from other battalions.

sentences.zh: 輪派二百名打靶，操演陣式。

translations.literal: Rotate two hundred for target practice and drill in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Rotate two hundred men for target practice and formation drills.

sentences.zh: 」詔議行。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，調禮部尚書，又調吏部，實授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Minister of Rites, then to Personnel, and formally appointed Commander of the Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1842 he was transferred to Minister of Rites, then Personnel, and formally appointed Commander of the Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 上御閱武樓，親閱圓明園兵丁槍操，步式整齊，施放有準，嘉恩桂督率有方，賜花翎。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended the Military Review Tower and personally reviewed the Old Summer Palace soldiers' musket drill; their steps were orderly and firing accurate—Engui's supervision was praised as effective and peacock feathers were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reviewed Old Summer Palace musket drills from the Military Review Tower; troops marched in perfect order and fired accurately—Engui received peacock feathers for effective command.

sentences.zh: 時議節冗費，恩桂先已奏裁上駟院馬六百餘匹。

translations.literal: At the time economy of redundant expenses was discussed; Engui had already memorialized to cut more than six hundred horses from the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: As economy measures were debated, Engui had already memorialized to cut over six hundred Imperial Stud horses.

sentences.zh: 又奏言南苑六圈，請裁其二，並裁各圈及京圈馬二百餘匹。

translations.literal: He also memorialized that of the six enclosures of the Southern Park, two should be cut, and more than two hundred horses from each enclosure and the capital enclosures cut as well.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed cutting two of the Southern Park's six enclosures and over two hundred horses from park and capital herds.

sentences.zh: 上駟院、司鞍、司轡、蒙古醫生舊支馬乾銀，均減半給，如議行。

translations.literal: The Imperial Stud, Saddle Office, Harness Office, and Mongol physicians' former horse-forage silver payments were all halved, as deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-forage payments to the Imperial Stud, Saddle Office, Harness Office, and Mongol physicians were halved as proposed.

sentences.zh: 以兼攝事繁，罷管內務府，二十五年，復之。

translations.literal: Because concurrent duties were numerous, he was relieved of managing the Imperial Household; in the twenty-fifth year he resumed it.
translations.idiomatic: Relieved of Imperial Household duties due to overload, he resumed them in 1845.

sentences.zh: 恩桂在吏部，嚴杜冒濫。

translations.literal: At the Ministry of Personnel, Engui strictly blocked fraudulent appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At Personnel, Engui strictly blocked fraudulent appointments.

sentences.zh: 兼步軍統領衙門最久，先後逾十年，綜覈整頓，釐定章程，訓練兵卒，皆有實效，宣宗甚倚之。

translations.literal: He held concurrent charge of the Foot Soldiers command longest, altogether more than ten years; comprehensive scrutiny and reorganization, fixing regulations, training soldiers—all had real effect, and the Xuanzong Emperor relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the Foot Soldiers for over ten years—the longest tenure—reorganizing regulations and training troops with real effect; the Daoguang Emperor relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京察，特予議敘。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, in capital inspection, he was specially granted honors consideration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1846, capital inspection specially granted him honors.

sentences.zh: 又幸南苑，見草木牲畜蕃盛，嘉恩桂經理得宜，加一秩。

translations.literal: The Emperor again visited the Southern Park and saw plants and livestock flourishing; praising Engui's proper management, he added one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting the Southern Park again and seeing flourishing plants and livestock, the Emperor praised Engui's management and added one rank.

sentences.zh: 迭奉命治倉胥舞弊，及戶部捐納房書吏賄充司員、收受陋規諸獄，並持正不撓法。

translations.literal: Repeatedly by imperial command he handled granary clerks' fraud, and cases of Revenue Ministry donation-office clerks bribing to fill department posts and receiving improper fees—and throughout upheld the law without bending.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly ordered to prosecute granary clerks' fraud and Revenue Ministry donation-office bribery and improper fees, he upheld the law without compromise.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒於官，上深悼惜，稱其任勞任怨，殫竭血誠，贈太保，賜金治喪，諡文肅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died in office; the Emperor deeply mourned and lamented, praising his bearing labor and resentment and exhausting his loyal blood; he was given Grand Preceptor, gold for funeral arrangements, and posthumously titled Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in 1848; the Emperor deeply mourned him, praising his willingness to bear hardship and his wholehearted dedication; he was posthumously titled Grand Preceptor Wensu, with gold granted for his funeral.

sentences.zh: =【論】=論曰：姚文田建言切中時弊，戴敦元清介幹事，其風概越流俗矣。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Yao Wentian's memorials struck at the abuses of the age; Dai Dunyuan was pure, upright, and capable in affairs—their bearing surpassed the vulgar current.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Yao Wentian's memorials struck at contemporary abuses; Dai Dunyuan was incorruptible and capable—their character rose above the common run.

sentences.zh: 朱士彥之治河，何凌漢之掌計，李振祜之執法，並號稱職。

translations.literal: Zhu Shiyan's management of rivers, He Linghan's charge of accounts, and Li Zhenhu's enforcement of law were all acclaimed as fulfilling duty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shiyan's river management, He Linghan's fiscal stewardship, and Li Zhenhu's law enforcement were all acclaimed as dutiful service.

sentences.zh: 恩桂奏績金吾，肅清輦轂，一時稱矯矯焉。

translations.literal: Engui reported achievements as commander of the capital guard, purifying the imperial precincts—for a time he was called outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Engui distinguished himself commanding the capital guard and securing the imperial precincts—at the time he was hailed as outstanding among his peers.
